newsitem.title: NIGERIA: PZ drop depresses Nigerian share index.
newsitem.headline: PZ drop depresses Nigerian share index.

text.p: Shares of conglomerate PZ Industries tumbled in Tuesday's trading at the Nigerian stock market, sending the all-share index lower despite appreciable gains by most other blue chips.
A 50 kobo drop in the price of PZ Industries, the Nigerian bourse's most capitalised stock, caused the index to close at 7314.10 from 7334.56 on Monday.
"Investors who are selling to take profit following a recent bonus issue are responsible for the drop," one trader said.

Rising stocks were still in a dominant position as demand continued to soar, traders said. Union Bank, one of the country's top three, posted an impressive full-year result which boosted its price on Tuesday to 9.20 naira, a 40 kobo gain.
Its after-tax profit to end-September 1996 shot up to 1.1 billion naira from 575 million naira a year earlier.
In anticipation of a good result, First Bank gained 25 kobo to 10.15 naira, the same as UBA which closed at 8.25 naira.
Also on the rise were food and oil marketers. Nestle was 40 kobo better at 57.50 naira, Cadbury went 20 kobo higher at 25.40 naira and Total rose to 65.40 naira, up 20 kobo.
Other losers included packaging firm Van Leer which finished 20 kobo down at 11.30 naira and Ashaka Cement, five kobo down at 13.85 naira.
